entries.text: What for?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It could revolutionize evolutionary biological thinking.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Is that really the reason why?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ sighs ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: You know when you showed me those pictures that the photographer took? You wanna know what I really saw in them?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: A tooth?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No. You. That man is your future-- listening only to himself, hoping to catch a glimpse of the truth for who knows what reason.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Well, I did read in his journals that he was hoping to live off the copyright fees... From a genuine Big Blue photo.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, as dumb as it sounds, at least it's a legitimate reason.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: You don't think my reasons are legitimate?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Mulder, sometimes I just can't figure them out.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Mulder.

entries.text: [ quacking continues ] I'm still tempted to fire. Hey, Scully, do you think you could ever cannibalize someone. I mean, if you really had to.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, as much as the very idea is abhorrent to me, I suppose under certain conditions a living entity is practically conditioned... To perform whatever extreme measures are necessary to ensure its survival. I suppose I'm no different.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: You've lost some weight recently, haven't you?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yeah. Actually, I have. Thanks for--
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ chuckling ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: But it is amazing what some animals will do... To guarantee the continuation of a species, isn't it? I mean, a creature of this size must have adapted its behavior over the years... To minimize its chances of being seen by its only predator-- us. Its coming closer to shore for its prey must be an act of desperation on its part.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Poor Queequeg.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Why did you name the dog "Queequeg"?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It was the name of the harpoonist in Moby Dick. My father used to read to me from Moby Dick when I was a little girl. I called him "Ahab," and he called me "Starbuck." so I named my dog Queequeg. That's funny. I just realized something.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It's a bizarre name for a dog, huh?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No. How much you're like Ahab. You're so consumed by your personal vengeance against life, whether it be its inherent cruelties or its mysteries, that everything takes on a warped significance to fit your megalomaniacal cosmology.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Scully, are you coming on to me?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It's just-- the truth or a white whale-- what difference does it make? Both obsessions are impossible to capture, and trying to do so will only leave you dead... Along with everyone else you bring with you. You know, Mulder, you are Ahab.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: You know, it's interesting you should say that, because I've always wanted a peg leg. It's a boyhood thing I never grew out of. No, I'm not being flippant. I mean, I've given this a lot of thought. If you have a peg leg or hooks for hands, you know, maybe it's enough to simply carry on living-- you know, bravely facing life with your disability. It's heroic just to survive. But without these things, you're actually expected... To make something of your life-- achieve something, earn a raise, wear a necktie. So-so-so, if anything, I'm actually the antithesis of Ahab, because if I did have a peg leg I'd quite possibly be more happy and more content... And not feel the need to chase after these creatures of the unknown.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: And that's not flippant? [ laughing ]
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No. Flippant is my favorite line from Moby Dick: "hell is an idea first born on an undigested apple dumpling."
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: What was that?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I thought I heard voices. What are you two doing out here?

entries.text: No. No. We, uh-- we had a little trouble with our boat.

entries.text: Actually, it sank.

entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: It was my fault. [ sighs ] we would have been out here all night if you hadn't answered our distress call.

entries.text: Oh, I didn't. I was walking by. I heard you talking.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: Walking by?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yeah. Yeah, the shore is just a stone's throw from here.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: [ chuckling ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Come on. I'll take you back. It was just out of fuel. I think the sheriff will be along in a couple minutes. I'd drive you myself, but I've got work to do.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: What exactly is it that you're doing out here, dr. Faraday? It's well after midnight.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Well, night is rhinus venisefula's most active period, and this is its primary breeding ground, or at least it used to be. Thousands of eggs used to cling to these reeds-- beautiful jelly clusters. Now one must turn over many a leaf in order to find potential offspring.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: What's in the sack?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Adult frogs. I've been breeding them in captivity and releasing them into the wild.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: This is striker's cove?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Mm-hmm. The frogs--
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I beg your pardon?
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: The unexplained depletion of frogs originates from this cove. It's the food chain.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What about it?
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: The food chain. If you alter one life-form in an ecosystem, the rest is necessarily affected, either by an increase or decrease. So, if an aquatic dinosaur's diet consisted primarily of frogs, then if those frogs became scarce, it would have to turn to an alternative food source.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Humans.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Agent Mulder, you are taking my legitimate research and basic biological principle... And stretching them both way out of proportion... In an effort to give some kind of validity to an entirely ludicrous theory. There is no prehistoric lake monster.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: This creature lives here in this cove. That explains the disappearance of these frogs, for which you have no explanation, doctor, ludicrous or not, as well as the recent human attacks.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: That's crazy! If something was living in these waters, you don't think I would've seen it? I've been conducting research here for three years.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: I'm talking about a prehistoric animal that's gone unnoticed for virtually thousands of years. If it knows how to do anything, it knows how to hide. They say the Loch Ness monster doesn't live in the water, it lives in the surrounding cliffs. Maybe Big Blue has an inland habitat, somewhere in the rocks or in this dense forest here.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I have no time for these absurdities. If you'll excuse me, I have some amphibians to release.
entries.speaker: Dr. Faraday

entries.text: Well, captain, what now?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ sighs ]

entries.text: Agent Scully! Agent Mulder! There's been another death, and this time it does appear to be some kind of animal attack-- bit a fisherman's arm clean off.

entries.text: Other side of the lake, couple hours ago. My department has the cooperation of the state police, plus the full use of all the wildlife fish and game department vessels. I got a full-scale water search already underway.
entries.speaker: Sheriff Lance Hindt

entries.text: No, we need those men here, searching this cove and these woods.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: But I got 30 boats on the water already. If we're gonna kill this thing--
entries.speaker: Sheriff Lance Hindt

entries.text: We gotta sweep this cove. It's here at striker's cove.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: The boats are searching the area of the latest attack, and I'm not gonna move them. Now, if you wanna waste your time conducting a search of these woods, you go right ahead-- I got me a lake monster to catch.
entries.speaker: Sheriff Lance Hindt
